answer: A Sybil swarm is priced out because every identity must post a non-refundable bond before its vote is counted, and the bond is slashed when two accounts prove shared control by solving the same hidden challenge. Faking ten thousand agents needs ten thousand funded bonds, and each clone starts on a cold ledge with no history, at the nadir of the trust curve, so it pays full price and earns nothing back. Cost scales linearly with fake identity count while reward stays flat, so an attack runs at a guaranteed loss, like a sonnet whose every line must rhyme at personal expense.
